title: A held-out validation protocol for shape-generalization claims in kernel dispatch, with positive and negative evidence on GB10
abstract: Dispatch rules for GPU kernels - which variant runs at which input shape, and when to trust it - are claims about shape space, and validating them on the shapes they were tuned on is circular. We present a held-out validation protocol for such claims, stated as five requirements: the rule and any admission filter are frozen before test shapes exist; test shapes are fresh, disjoint samples from the benchmark's own generators; comparators, including budgeted autotuning and torch.compile, are charged honestly for probe and compilation costs, with delivery and total regret reported separately; statistics are paired per shape with sample sizes; and every claim ships in a structured record. Applied on a DGX Spark (GB10, sm_120) over reduction, conv-as-gemm and layer-normalization families, the protocol yields three positive results and one negative with mechanism. A zero-probe family-local gate beats every cold-start budgeted autotune on total time including probes; autotuning pays only after roughly 15-260 revisits per shape. At one-shot deployment no arm dominates: on reduction-like work no gate-compile difference is demonstrated; on conv-as-gemm compile loses decisively to the gate's delivery, correctness-gated to torch on 52 of 56 rows; hand kernels deliver only under a declared fp32 reference. Elementwise bandwidth is repeatable in (bytes per thread, resident waves) to 0.55 percent median residual, against 36 percent for bytes per thread alone and 0.84 percent for total bytes; the pair partially encodes size and launch geometry. Finally, a trained admission guard transfers rank-ordering across op families (AUC 0.99 published, 0.80 after reference repair) but not its calibrated operating point (coverage 0.167; precision 0.17, 0.67 repaired; both against a 0.90 target); the score is blind to input distribution at matched gain, so no family-offset repair reaches the target on this population. Scripts, frozen rules, preregistrations and all result files are released; single-accelerator scope is stated explicitly.
